summary.title: Build a Simple Weather App With Vanilla JavaScript
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a card-based weather search app with plain HTML, CSS Grid and JavaScript, fetching data from the OpenWeatherMap API with the Fetch API and preventing duplicate city requests.
keywords: build a weather website with javascript
takeaways: Structure a search form and a dynamically populated list of city cards in HTML and CSS.
Call the OpenWeatherMap weather endpoint with a city name, API key and metric units using fetch() and response.json().
Build list item markup from the API response, including the icon URL derived from the weather icon code.
Avoid duplicate requests by comparing the search input with existing city names and data-name attributes.
summary.summary: This Envato Tuts+ tutorial walks through building a simple weather search app using vanilla JavaScript. It covers scaffolding with an OpenWeatherMap API key, writing the markup and CSS (variables, responsive grid of cards), and then the JavaScript: handling form submission, calling the API with fetch, and generating a city card from the response. It also replaces the default icons with custom SVGs and adds logic to prevent duplicate requests for the same city and country. The article notes the One Call API 2.5 it uses has been deprecated and includes a sponsored weatherstack section.
